title.rendered: I Am the Righteousness of God in Christ: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God. Not might earn. Not might work toward. Might become. This is who you are in Christ.

content.rendered:
God made Him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God. Not might earn. Not might work toward. Might become. This is the most underestimated sentence in the New Testament.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, June 30, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.”
2 Corinthians 5:21 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Yesterday we saw that the believer is a new creation. Today we see what kind of new creation. Paul says the believer has become the righteousness of God in Christ. Read that again slowly. Not has access to God’s righteousness. Not is working toward God’s righteousness. Has become it. This is not metaphor. This is the legal and spiritual reality of the believer’s standing before God.

The verse is structured as the great exchange. Jesus, who had no sin of His own, was made to be sin on the cross. He took on what belonged to us. In return, the believer is made the righteousness of God. We have taken on what belongs to Him. It is, as the old hymn says, the sweetest exchange in all of history. He took our sin. We took His righteousness. The transaction is settled.

This matters because most believers spend their entire Christian life trying to feel righteous rather than knowing they are righteous. They base their sense of standing with God on how they performed in their devotional time, how their week has gone, whether they were patient with their children, whether they prayed enough this morning. Paul cuts through all of it. Your righteousness is not a feeling. It is not a performance. It is a position. You are the righteousness of God in Christ. Today. Right now. Whether you feel like it or not.

The implications are enormous. The believer who knows this can pray with confidence because they know their standing is settled. They can serve without trying to earn favour because they know the favour is already there. They can fail and recover quickly because their identity does not collapse with one mistake. They can hear correction from the Holy Spirit without being crushed by condemnation because they know the correction comes from a Father who has already declared them righteous in Christ.

This is the second great truth of who you are in Christ. You are not trying to become righteous. You have become the righteousness of God in Him. Walk in it today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I am the righteousness of God in Christ. I did not earn this and I cannot lose it. Jesus was made sin for me. In Him I have been made the righteousness of God. This is my position before You today, settled and unshakable. I stand in Your presence not because of my performance but because of His finished work. I walk through this day in the righteousness that has been given to me, free, bold, and at peace with You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am the righteousness of God in Christ Jesus. My standing before God is settled. I did not earn it. I cannot lose it. I walk in His righteousness today.
